who_imnci_danger_signs_under5.label: Unable to drink or breastfeed
who_imnci_danger_signs_under5.description: Child cannot suck or swallow liquids

who_imnci_danger_signs_under5.label: Vomits everything
who_imnci_danger_signs_under5.description: Child cannot retain any food or fluids

who_imnci_danger_signs_under5.label: Convulsions or fits (current or during illness)
Lethargic or unconscious / abnormally sleepy
who_imnci_danger_signs_under5.description: Child is difficult to awaken or non-responsive

who_imnci_danger_signs_under5.label: Subcostal chest indrawing
who_imnci_danger_signs_under5.description: Lower chest wall pulls inward during inhalation

who_imnci_danger_signs_under5.label: Stridor in a calm child
who_imnci_danger_signs_under5.description: Harsh inspiratory sound when not crying

who_imnci_danger_signs_under5.label: Signs of severe dehydration
who_imnci_danger_signs_under5.description: Sunken eyes, skin pinch takes >2 seconds to return

who_imnci_danger_signs_under5.label: Blood in stool (dysentery signs)
who_imnci_danger_signs_under5.description: Visible fresh blood in watery or loose stool

pregnancy_red_flags.label: Severe persistent headache with high blood pressure (>=140/90)
Blurred vision, seeing spots, or photophobia
Convulsions, fits, or loss of consciousness
Heavy vaginal bleeding (soaking pad within 1 hour)
Severe continuous abdominal or epigastric pain
Reduced or absent fetal movements (after 24 weeks)
High fever with chills or foul vaginal discharge
Sudden gush or continuous leaking of watery fluid
Sudden severe swelling of face, eyes, or hands
Difficulty breathing or acute chest pain
